note: The desired state a directory read of users_page1, users_page2, groups_page1 and groups_page2 yields, corpus-local because deriving it is IdP-agnostic work the planner already owns for Entra. Subjects are user uuids throughout (sub_mode user_uuid): the wire names members by integer pk inside a group's users array, and this has already mapped every such pk to the member's uuid. The population is narrowed to the admission closure -- the groups reachable from kb-admission by following child-group edges (kb-admission, kb-mid, kb-inner, kb-two-parents, kb-cyc-a, kb-cyc-b), plus the users those selected groups hold. That is why the four pages carry 13 users and 11 groups while this carries 5 and 6: the filler groups, authentik's own three accounts and every unheld person are read but not admitted, and get no account. Every structural case survives the narrowing: kb-svc-sync is a held service account, kb-svc-retired a held disabled account (enabled false), kb-admission reaches kb-inner through kb-mid (two levels), kb-two-parents is a child of both kb-admission and kb-mid, and kb-cyc-a and kb-cyc-b name each other (the closure expands each selected group once and the second arrival is a no-op). name_candidates are username, then the dotted display name, then the address local part, each reduced by the shared name rule and dropped when nothing survives, deduplicated first-wins -- so a user whose three spellings collapse keeps one, and kb-svc-sync keeps its username and its dotted display name cut to the 20-character budget ('kerbridge.sync.colle') but nothing from its empty address. membership values list each selected group's held users first (in wire order) then its selected child groups; a member group the closure did not select is not named here. refused is empty: no adapter rule turns an authentik account away, so no held account is refused.
